## Topic and Questions

- [x] Pick a topic the team is genuinely interested in
- [x] Come up with 1–3 clear, answerable research questions

Our topic: **Video game film adaptations**

1. Do critics and audiences agree on video game movies, and has that gap changed over time?
2. Does publisher franchise power predict box office success?
3. Does franchise fatigue exist in video game movies?

---

## Data

- [x] Primary source: TidyTuesday CSV (not the R package) — [game_films.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-06-09/game_films.csv)
- [x] Supplementary sources (CPI table, FX rates, publisher revenue) — note provenance
- [x] Read in, tidy, wrangle, clean
- [x] Describe data provenance: where, who, why, what are the cases (one row = one film)

---

## Report Requirements

### Format
- [x] Quarto, output as **PDF**
- [x] Code in **Code Appendix** at the end (use `ref.label` snippet)
- [x] Body = narrative + figures + tables (no raw code)

### Length
- [x] Body ≥ 10 pages (title page, references, appendix don't count)

### Figures & Tables
- [x] ≥ 3 figures (plots)
- [x] ≥ 1 non-trivial table (summary/aggregation, not raw data dump)
- [x] ≥ 1 figure with 3+ variables (color, facets, size, shape)
- [x] Every figure/table: caption + cross-reference by number from narrative
- [x] Each figure/table: a few sentences of discussion

### Required Sections (in order)
- [x] **Title block**: report title, all team members, date
- [x] **Introduction & Motivation**: what and why
- [x] **Research Question(s)**: 1–3 questions, numbered/labeled
- [x] **Data Provenance**: source, collector, cases, key variables (with units)
- [x] **Data Wrangling & Cleaning**: narrative of import/tidy/join/clean decisions
- [x] **Exploratory Data Analysis**: figures, table(s), discussion
- [x] **Findings / Conclusions**: answers tied back to research questions
- [x] **Limitations & Future Work**: gaps, what you'd do with more time/data
- [x] **AI Use Statement**: 1–2 sentences per member or team paragraph
- [x] **References**: APA/MLA/footnotes
- [x] **Code Appendix**: `{{r codeAppend, ref.label=knitr::all_labels(), echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}}`

### Citations
- [x] Cite data sources
- [x] Cite any adapted code

---

## Reproducibility

- [x] GitHub repository for the project
- [x] README explaining how to reproduce
- [x] Final report renders cleanly from repo on someone else's machine

---

## AI Policy

- [x] AI use note in final report
- [x] Each team member can walk through their own code at oral checkpoints
